44843.title: A Work Order number matches exactly with or without the dash or a space
44843.refs: SV-9160 (PRD 7 (S2-15276 = s215276); identifier fields are exact-only)
44843.custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search, which searches across work orders, customers, parts and more; results appear grouped by type under a tab strip.
1. A Work Order 'S2-15276' exists.
44843.custom_steps:
1. In the search box, type 'S2-15276' and read the result.
2. Clear the input and type 'S215276' (no dash) and read the result.
3. Clear the input and type 'S2 15276' (with a space) and read the result.
44843.custom_expected:
All three forms find the same Work Order 'S2-15276'.

The Work Order number is treated as an identifier: it is normalized by stripping the dash/space, so 'S2-15276' equals 's215276'.

The match is exact (identifier), not fuzzy.

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945), section 7 (S2-15276 = s215276); identifier fields are exact-only, read on 16 September 2026.

Last checked against build v26.36.7-21b4db9 on 9/16/2026.

44847.title: Typos in identifier fields do NOT return fuzzy matches
44847.refs: SV-9160 (PRD 7 (exact identifier fields bypass fuzzy logic))
44847.custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search, which searches across work orders, customers, parts and more; results appear grouped by type under a tab strip.
1. A Work Order 'S2-15276' exists and no Work Order 'S2-15286' exists.
44847.custom_steps:
1. In the search box, type a near-miss Work Order number, for example 'S2-15286' (one digit off from a real WO).
2. Read the result rows and the group headings in the results list.
44847.custom_expected:
The real Work Order 'S2-15276' is NOT returned as a fuzzy match.

Because identifier fields are exact-only, a one-digit-off WO number returns no fuzzy identifier match (it may show 'No results' if nothing else matches).

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945), section 7 (exact identifier fields bypass fuzzy logic), read on 16 September 2026.

Last checked against build v26.36.7-21b4db9 on 9/16/2026.

55684.title: After switching location you never see the old location's records
55684.refs: SV-9160 (INV-94; V1 baseline 55767168; no stale rows in flight)
55684.custom_preconds:
BEFORE YOU START — a five-second check that the test data is there. Open global search and type ZZAUTOTEST. You should get several groups of results — Work orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part sales.
If you get nothing at all, a new build has wiped our test data. Stop, and ask for the test data to be put back — it is one command and takes about a minute.
Do NOT create the records yourself. Records made by hand come out slightly different every time — a different postcode, a different spelling — and a test that passes against the wrong data is worse than one that fails, because it tells you everything is fine when nothing was really checked.
You only need this check ONCE at the start of a testing session, not before every case.

1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header click the Search box (it is a BUTTON, data-test-id global_search_trigger, not a typeable field) or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K. Global search opens as a CENTRED MODAL over the page: a text input at the top, then a scope tab strip - All, Work orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part sales, Purchase orders, Vendor invoices - each showing its own result count, then results grouped by type with a count beside each heading (e.g. "Work orders (4)"). Esc closes the modal. NOTE: group headings are SENTENCE case in the build ("Work orders", "Part sales"). If a group shows nothing, click that entity's scope tab to confirm it really is 0 rather than scrolling. Modal behaviour verified on the V2 QA branch sv9160 on 14 September 2026.
1. You are signed in as a user with access to BOTH locations - Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
2. You are currently on Heavy Duty.
3. The four ZZAUTOTEST work orders belong to Heavy Duty and to customer 'ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling'. Lethbridge has none of them.

HOW TO GET A WORK ORDER NUMBER TO TYPE — do this first, it takes five seconds. Open global search and type ZZAUTOTEST. The Work orders group lists our four test jobs. Write down the number of any one of them — it looks like S-17611. Use THAT number wherever these steps say "the work order number". Why you are asked to look it up instead of being given one: the job numbers change every time a new build is put on this branch, so any number printed here would be wrong within days. The number on screen is always right.
55684.custom_steps:
1. On Heavy Duty, open global search and type: Bridgeport
2. Confirm the four work orders appear.
3. WITHOUT closing search, switch the location to Lethbridge.
4. Search Bridgeport again and watch the results CLOSELY as they load - including the moment before the new results settle.
5. Repeat the switch a few times, watching each time.
55684.custom_expected:
After the switch, the Heavy Duty work orders are gone and they are never shown even for a moment while the new results are loading.
The customer itself still appears at both locations - customers belong to the whole company - but its WORK ORDERS belong to Heavy Duty and must not follow you to Lethbridge, not even briefly.
In V1 the old location's rows were cleared the instant you switched, before the new ones were fetched, precisely so nothing from the other location could flash on screen. A brief flash is still a user seeing records from a location they have switched away from.
IF THIS FAILS: it is a real V1-to-V2 capability loss. Mark the test FAILED and write down the exact words you typed and what came back. It worked in the previous version, so it has to work here - failing is a fault and a ticket is raised against it. Do not pass the test just because the newer specification allows the new behaviour.

---
SOURCE - THIS CASE IS TESTED AGAINST V1, NOT AGAINST THE V2 SPECIFICATION.
This is the expected behaviour as per the V1 product itself: the ShopView product repository at commit 55767168, useGlobalSearch.ts:286-299, which empties the collection and the recent list on a location switch BEFORE re-fetching - and V1's own test 'drops the previous location rows while the re-fetch is in flight' asserts exactly this.
For this V1 regression suite the shipped V1 product IS the specification (Standing Rule 109). Epic SV-9160 is the project this work belongs to, not the source of this expectation, and anything quoted below from the V2 requirements is context only - never the authority for this case.. Version 1.5 of the specification (Confluence page 576978945) requires results to follow the current location; it does not describe what is shown while the switch is in progress.
Standing Rule 96 makes a V1 capability the default expectation and Standing Rule 58 makes a code-versus-document conflict a PO DECISION ITEM, so this case asserts the V1 behaviour and tells you to record and flag rather than guess.
